- Precatorius : Relating to prayer (Abrus precatorius seeds are used as rosary beads).

seed.text: There are 3-8 polished and hard seeds in a pod. The seeds are nearly globose, 6-7 mm long, scarlet coloured with black lateral spot at the base (around the hilum). Sometimes the seeds are black with a white eye and more rarely pure white.

fruit.text: The fruit is a short, oblong, pilose (finely silky), winkled and thick pod , 3-4 cm long and 1-1.5 cm wide. It is turgid with a sharp deflexed beak. This pod splits before falling to reveal the seeds.

This pod splits before falling to reveal the seeds.

flower.text: The flowers are crowded in dense clusters, terminal or axillary. They are clustered at the swollen nodes of the rachis. This pseudo-raceme is 10 cm long (shorter than leaves) and has a 3 cm long peduncle . The flowers are 1 cm across, shortly stalked (2 mm long pedicel ). The bracts are deciduous and bracteols are appressed to the calyx. The calyx tube is narrowly campanulate, pubescent (likely silky), 2-3 mm long with a truncate apex and very short and obscure lobes. The corolla is composed of clawed, white to pink or pale violet petals . The standard (banner) is broadly ovate, auricled, 1.5 cm long and 0.8-1 cm wide. The standard base is adherent to the staminal sheath. The wings are narrow, oblong and falcate, 0.8 cm long and 0.3-0.4 cm wide. The keels are curved, 1 cm long and 0.2-0.3 cm wide. The stamina sheath is 8 mm long. Androecium is composed of 9 monodelphuous stamens with nearly equal filaments (2-3 mm long) and uniform anthers. The pistil is composed of a 8 mm sub-sessile and pubescent ovary, a very short (0.5 mm) and incurved style with a capitate stigma.

leaf.text: The leaves are alternate, petioled (1 cm long petiole), 10-15 cm long, even-pinnately compound with 10-15 pairs of leaflets. The leaflets are opposite, oblong, thinly membranous, slightly hairy, 1.5-2.5 long and 0.6-0.8 cm wide, with margins entire, base and apex obtuse, apex apiculate. They terminate in a bristle and they have a 1-1.5 mm long petiolule . The rachis is thickened at the base, very slender, channeled and glabrous and ending in a spine. At the base of a leaf, there are small, setaceous and 2.5 mm long stipules .
leaf.text_html:
The leaves are alternate, petioled (1 cm long petiole), 10-15 cm long, even-pinnately compound with 10-15 pairs of leaflets.
The leaflets are opposite, oblong, thinly membranous, slightly hairy, 1.5-2.5 long and 0.6-0.8 cm wide, with margins entire, base and apex obtuse, apex apiculate. They terminate in a bristle and they have a 1-1.5 mm long petiolule.
The rachis is thickened at the base, very slender, channeled and glabrous and ending in a spine. 
At the base of a leaf, there are small, setaceous and 2.5 mm long stipules.

habit.text: Abrus precatorius is a deciduous, perennial and thornless climber . It is a high-climbing, twining, or trailing woody vine with slender herbaceous branches.
habit.text_html:

reproduction_dispersal.text: Bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures). The flowers are nectariferous. Pollination is through the agents of insects. Mechanical dispersal : barochory (dispersal of seeds by gravity), self-propagation. The seeds are also spread by birds.
reproduction_dispersal.text_html:
• Sex distribution :

    Bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures).

  • Mode of pollination :

    The flowers are nectariferous. Pollination is through the agents of insects.

  • Seed dispersal :

    Mechanical dispersal : barochory (dispersal of seeds by gravity), self-propagation.
    The seeds are also spread by birds.

others.text: The oil made from Abrus precatorius seeds is sometimes used as an ingredient in Indian hair products.
others.text_html: The oil made from Abrus precatorius seeds is sometimes used as an ingredient in Indian hair products.

handicrafts.text: The seeds were used by jewellers as a unit of weight. The unit is known as ratti (the weight of one seed = 1 ratti and 8 ratti = 1 Gram). Formerly, Indians used this measure to weigh gold. The finely powdered seeds are used by jewellers to increase adhesion when soldering delicate ornaments. The seeds are used for making bracelets, necklaces, rosaries, etc. The fibre extracted from the stem is woven into baskets.
handicrafts.text_html:
The seeds were used by jewellers as a unit of weight. The unit is known as ratti (the weight of one seed = 1 ratti and 8 ratti = 1 Gram). Formerly, Indians used this measure to weigh gold.

The finely powdered seeds are used by jewellers to increase adhesion when soldering delicate ornaments. 

The seeds are used for making bracelets, necklaces, rosaries, etc. 

The fibre extracted from the stem is woven into baskets.

reforestation.text: Abrus precatorius can be planted in the sun or half shade and it will grow in a wide variety of situations and soils. 12 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
reforestation.text_html:
• Planting advice and requirements :

    Abrus precatorius can be planted in the sun or half shade and it will grow in a wide variety of situations and soils.

  • Seed treatments :

    12 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
